<!-- Capstone (path.yml form: capstone, `sandbox: SB<n>`; curriculum v2 §7.9, §16.3 and §3.4). Guide:
     assets/learn/README.md, "Sandboxes and capstones". Replace <slug> with the capstone's JS name and <id> with its
     path.yml id.
     Order: the brief (the decision, who it is for, the deliverable and when it is done, the time) -> the plan (the
     sandbox's engine with the capstone's choices: LX.BenchRun to run it, LX.ShareState for the plan link; the
     sensitivity chart, e.g. LX.Tornado, with the plan held fixed or re-sized, said in words) -> the note (LX.ReportNote:
     the reader's words, the plan's numbers, the assumptions, the sensitivity line and the limits as a one-page note to
     copy; its checks are the deliverable's "done when") -> the self-check (LX.Exemplars: a weak and a strong note for the
     same brief, illustrative; LX.Rubric: the competences the capstone builds, the course's words, a "look for" line
     each) -> sources. The step links are #brief, #plan, #note, #selfcheck and #sources (the build checks that each
     exists); the screenshot tool reaches them as sec-brief, sec-plan, sec-note, sec-selfcheck and sec-sources, and
     `explain` (and `open`) show #exemplars.
     Built on a sandbox: load the sandbox's engine (assets/learn/components/<engine>.js, in the bundle) and use its
     schema, presets, engine.solve (through LX.BenchRun), summarize and note (see _template-sandbox.qmd). Do not fork
     the engine: a capstone narrows the controls (which site, which choices) and adds its brief, its note fields and its
     rubric. The engine's failure states, tie rule and wording rules apply here unchanged.
     The deliverable (curriculum §7.9): the plan link, the one-page note with a sensitivity chart (the note carries the
     sensitivity line and table; the chart stays on the page), and for the Modeler version the notebook (a Go deeper box
     in #note with the allow-listed repository's Colab link). Nothing is saved or sent anywhere: the reader copies the
     note and the link, and the page says so (ReportNote's privacy line).
     Rubric (§3.4): pick the competences (C0 and C1: accounting, uncertainty, realism, communication) and add a "look
     for" line each; never reword the levels. The exemplars are illustrative and say so; they use the engine's real
     numbers for the default plan, checked by the test.
     Time: path.yml `minutes` is the whole capstone (60 for C0, 90 for C1); `lab_minutes` the Modeler notebook. Count the
     runs and the writing honestly.
     Scope (§20): the sites are fictional; data centers appear only as loads; Henry's research only through approved
     excerpts (held in learn/_drafts/ until approved, like a case file), allow-listed repositories and citations.
     After editing path.yml, run in the ResearchPortfolio folder:
     python3 scripts/build_learn.py --site <site>   (fills the three marker blocks below; never edit them by hand) -->

```{=html}
<!-- The brief sits above the interactive, outside every fallback, so readers see it with and without JavaScript.

<div class="lx-card lx-cap-brief">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">The brief</p>
<p class="lx-case-q">The decision, in one sentence, and who has to make it.</p>
<ol class="lx-studio-task">
<li><b>Hand in:</b> a plan link and a one-page note with a sensitivity line (Modeler version: the notebook too).</li>
<li><b>From:</b> the sandbox's engine (a link to the sandbox page) and the site's data, with its year.</li>
<li><b>Done when:</b> every check under the note is in place and the self-check reaches Proficient, in the rubric's words.</li>
</ol>
<p class="lx-hint">About N minutes: N to build and run the plan, N to write the note, N to check it.</p>
</div>
```

## Build and run your plan
:::

```{=html}
<!-- The live plan: the sandbox's bench frame (div.lx-sb: controls, then the run box with LX.BenchRun and

     above them) in #<slug>-results below it. The fallbacks are complete: the default plan, its precomputed results with
     the run's date, and how to do the task on paper. -->

<!-- <slug>-plan:start (written from engine.schema by LX.ShareState.staticHTML in the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->

<!-- <slug>-plan:end -->
```

## Write your one-page note

```{=html}
<!-- LX.ReportNote fills this: the reader's fields, the deliverable's checks and the note's preview, with "Copy as text"

     state ({ ok, stale }) from LX.BenchRun. The fallback is the note's outline, from the same fields. -->

<!-- <slug>-note:end -->
</div>
</div>
```
